title: The sheaf Hom of sheaves of modules is a sheaf of modules
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules. For an object $U$ let $H(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal G|_U)$ be the set of morphisms of sheaves of $\mathcal O_U$-modules on the localized site $\mathcal C/U$; it is an $\mathcal O(U)$-module, $\mathcal O(U)$ being the ring of global sections of $\mathcal O_U$ (the final object of $\mathcal C/U$ is $U/U$), by $(f\varphi)_{V/U}=f|_V\,\varphi_{V/U}$. For $a:V\to U$ let $H(U)\to H(V)$ send $\varphi$ to its restriction along the relocalization $\mathcal C/V\to\mathcal C/U$, i.e. $(\varphi|_V)_{W/V}=\varphi_{W/U}$. Then: (1) $H$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules on $\mathcal C$ (the restriction maps are semilinear over $\mathcal O(U)\to\mathcal O(V)$); (2) $H$ is a sheaf on $\mathcal C$; (3) $H(U)\cong\Gamma(\mathcal C/U,H|_U)$ and the global sections $\Gamma(\mathcal C,H)$ (compatible families of elements of the $H(U)$) are in bijection, $\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$-linearly, with $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$, a morphism $\varphi$ corresponding to the family $(\varphi|_U)_U$.

proof.text: For each U, define H(U)=Hom_{O|_U}(F|_U,G|_U), and for V→U restrict a morphism along the relocalization C/V→C/U. Multiplication by a section f∈O(U) is defined by multiplying the source or target; commutativity of O makes the two definitions agree, and restriction is semilinear over O(U)→O(V). This is the pointwise construction of the presheaf and module structure.

For every covering family of U, compatible local O-linear maps F|_{U_i}→G|_{U_i} glue uniquely to an O-linear map on C/U by [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing]; O-linearity is local because addition and scalar multiplication are sectionwise.
The localized site C/U has final object U/U, so a section of H over C/U is the same as an element of H(U); this gives H(U)≅Γ(C/U,H|_U), compatibly with restrictions and the O(U)-module structures.

A global section of H is a family (φ_U)_{U∈C}, φ_U∈H(U), with φ_U|_V=φ_V for every a:V→U, i.e. (φ_U)_{W/U}=(φ_V)_{W/V} for W→V→U [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Given such a family define φ:F→G by φ_V=(φ_V)_{V/V}:F(V)→G(V) (using F|_V(V/V)=F(V), G|_V(V/V)=G(V)). For a:W→V, compatibility gives (φ_V)_{W/V}=(φ_W)_{W/W}=φ_W, so naturality of φ_V for the morphism W/V→V/V of C/V is naturality of φ for a; each φ_V is O(V)-linear, so φ∈Hom_O(F,G). Conversely a morphism φ gives the compatible family (φ|_U)_U with (φ|_U)_{V/U}=φ_V. The two constructions are inverse: (φ|_V)_{V/V}=φ_V, and for a given family (φ_U)_{W/U}=(φ_W)_{W/W}, which is the W/U-component of the restriction to C/U of the morphism built from it. For s∈Γ(C,O) the family s·(φ_U)_U has components s_U φ_U, whose V/V-component is s_V(φ_V)_{V/V}; by the formula (sφ)_V(x)=s_Vφ_V(x) of [def-pur-sheaf-modules-hom-module] this is sφ, so the bijection is Γ(C,O)-linear. (Direct construction, no gluing: C need not have a final object, so the covering-gluing lemma does not apply here.)
